summary: Sydney Frank Markham was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Wadham College from circa 1923 to 1927 and served as Secretary and later President at the Museums Association around 1929 to 1942.

Syed Ali Bilgrami worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Patna College, Lucknow, Roorkee, London, and the Royal School of Mines. He served in the Government of Hyderabad (1879–1901) and became Reader in Marathi at Cambridge in 1901.

Syed Ameer Ali was a scholar in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Aliah University (1863–1867) and the University of Calcutta (1867–1869), where he later held a post from circa 1878 to 1881.

Historian and Indologist Syed Hasan Askari studied at Zila School Chapra, Langat Singh College, and Patna University. He succeeded Anant Sadashiv Altekar as Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute, serving from 1968 to 1971.
Syed Nawab Ali was a scholar of history and archaeology. In 1932, he was attested as Principal of Bahauddin College and Professor of Persian at the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda.
Sylvain Brocquet is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1980 under Marie-Claude Porcher. He later held an academic post at Aix-Marseille University.

Sylvain Lévi studied at the Sorbonne under Abel Bergaigne. A specialist in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he held major posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the Collège de France.

Sylvie Hureau specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. She held a post as maître de conférences at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2012) and was attested as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies in 2026.

Sze-bong Tso specialized in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed a PhD at the Australian National University (1977–1982), where he studied under doctoral supervisors Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.

Sámuel Brassai studied at János Zsigmond Unitarian Highschool and worked in linguistics, Indology, and philosophy. He held professorships at the John Sigismund Unitarian Academy, the Ludovika Military Academy, and Franz Joseph University (1872–1884).

Sándor Kégl earned his Ph.D. at Eötvös Loránd University (~1884–1889) under Ignác Goldziher and Ármin Vámbéry. A scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he became Privatdozent of Persian there in 1893.

Specializing in Tibetology and linguistics, Sándor Kőrösi Csoma studied at Bethlen Gábor College, the University of Göttingen under Johann Gottfried Eichhorn, and under Tibetan teachers including Sangye Phuntsok. He served as Librarian of The Asiatic Society (1837–1841).
Søren Ludvig Tuxen was educated at Østre Borgerdyd school until 1868 and later held a post at the same school in 1875.

Søren Sørensen studied at the University of Copenhagen (Ph.D. 1883) under Hammerich, Madvig, and Westergaard. A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he taught at Herlufsholm School and became Docent at the University of Copenhagen in 1899.
Sāmaṇera Bodhesako worked in Buddhist studies. He founded Path Press and held a post as an editor at the Buddhist Publication Society.
Sīlaratano studied under Narada Maha Thera, Ajahn Maha Bua, and Nyanaponika Thera.

T. Chandrasekharan was an Indologist who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He succeeded T. R. Chintamani and was attested in 1951 as Professor of History of Sanskrit Language and Literature at Madras Sanskrit College.

Indologist T. Ganapati Sastri earned a Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Tübingen. From circa 1908 to 1924, he served as Curator of the Department of Oriental Manuscripts Publications and Editor of the Trivandrum Sanskrit Series.

T. Griffith Foulk studied at the University of Michigan (PhD 1978–1987) under Luis Oscar Gómez. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology, he taught at the University of Michigan and later held professorships at Sarah Lawrence College.
T. K. V. Desikachar worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, studying under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya from circa 1961 to 1989. In 1976, he founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram.
